description: We are three inquisitive young people from Dushanbe, Tajikistan. We share a passion for space, science, and technology. We believe that NASA's open data can help solve real-world problems, from climate change to food security. Our team has programming, data analysis, and design skills, and we want to learn something new in 48 hours, create something useful, and turn data into solutions for people.
summary:
WhatCropNext — what to plant next. We developed an interactive crop rotation planner powered by 20 years of NASA POWER daily weather data. A farmer picks a field on a satellite map, drags crops onto a 4-year plan and, in under a second, sees what happens to yield, water use, income and soil health on a living, animated field. Every plan is tested against 20 real weather years, so the farmer sees reliability (“a good harvest in 15 of 20 similar years”), not a single guess. “What if” scenarios stress-test plans for a hotter, drier climate.

This addresses the Field Shift challenge by turning NASA climate data into a concrete adaptation decision. In Tajikistan’s Hissar Valley, where cotton has followed cotton for years, the tool shows how adding chickpea and switching to drip irrigation cuts water use by 32% and stops soil decline. That matters for millions of smallholder farmers in dry regions who face climate change without data or advisors.
details:
What it does. WhatCropNext helps farmers decide what to plant next. The user picks a field (Hissar Valley in Tajikistan, Iowa, Punjab, Kenya, or their own field drawn on a satellite image). The app builds a field passport from 20 years of NASA POWER daily weather, SoilGrids soil data, slope, MODIS vegetation data and a recent Sentinel-2 image, explained in plain language ("78 days a year above 35 °C"). The farmer then drags seed packets of 17 crops, including winter cover crops, onto a 4-year plan.

How it works. A day-by-day field model simulates soil moisture, crop growth by stage, heat, drought and frost stress, nitrogen, organic matter, erosion, and pest pressure when crops of the same family repeat. Soil state carries over from year to year. Each plan is run against 20 real weather years to show reliability, and "What if" scenarios (+1.5 °C and drier, dry spring, more heat) stress-test it. Irrigation type (rain-fed, furrow, drip), salinization risk, budget and labor are included. The output is an agronomist-style plan with yields, sowing dates, a work calendar and an on-site checklist, downloadable as PDF.

Benefits and impact. Lower water and fertilizer use, healthier soil and lower crop failure risk. Example: for cotton in the Hissar Valley, switching to drip irrigation cuts water use by 32% (4,930 vs 7,290 m³/ha) and removes salinization risk, while a chickpea year reduces nitrogen fertilizer needs. Target users are smallholders in dry irrigated regions such as Central Asia, agronomists and agriculture students.

Creativity. Instead of tables, the farmer plays with a living field: plants grow, the soil profile changes color, and four gauges (rain gauge, coins, soil auger, barometer) react in under a second. "Live 4 years" plays seasons week by week with model captions.

Factors we considered. Honesty: every number links to its source or is marked as an estimate, and every screen lists what to check on site. Accessibility: English, Russian and Tajik, lightweight SVG graphics that work on phones, offline cache.

Tools. Python (FastAPI), React + TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, SVG, Docker; data from NASA POWER, MODIS, Sentinel-2, SoilGrids, FAO-56, FAO EcoCrop, World Bank. Much of the code was generated with Claude (Anthropic) from our team's prompts and then reviewed and tested by the team; details are in the README.

What's next. Connecting NASA Earthdata layers (GPM IMERG rainfall, SMAP soil moisture, ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration, GRACE-FO groundwater), testing with farmers and agronomists in Tajikistan, adding local crop varieties and prices, and a mobile version for use in the field.

Live demo: https://frontend-production-ca7a5d62.up.railway.app/

Source code: https://github.com/ac9788737-commits/projectforSpaceApps
